findings.message: Instance fix (B1). The credential is now removed only inside the amax plugin. The server still accepts a repo URL that contains a username or token, and the MCP server writes every call's raw args to the append-only core.trace_event before the tool runs (packages/mcp/src/server.ts:41). Two paths still store a token permanently: (1) `link_project_repo` (mcp.ts:90, chat intent chat.ts:11), where a PM types or pastes the repo URL; (2) any other MCP client calling `sync_specclaw`. There is also a second copy of the stripping logic: `withoutCredentials` in the plugin and `normaliseRepo` on the server (B4). Fix: redact the userinfo part of URL-shaped args before the trace step writes them, or reject any repoUrl that contains userinfo in both tools' input schemas. Also add a test that calls the tool and then checks the trace row.
findings.scenario: A PM tells chat to link FLT to https://x-access-token:ghp_abc@github.com/example/fleet. link_project_repo stores the normalised URL, but core.trace_event keeps `ghp_abc` permanently.

findings.message: This only partly fixes last round's lagging-branch finding. Comparing commit times does not tell you whether a branch includes main's changes. Say a branch was cut from an older main, and a later commit on it touches only another change. Its commit time is newer, so every other proposal in the push passes the stale check. Its older title, tasksTotal, lane, acs and the rest of meta then overwrite what main had already synced. Only phase, pr and verdict are protected. The new SKILL.md step 4 makes this worse: `--apply` now applies unattended whenever the other skips are 'would move back' or 'stale', so the field regressions are applied with no review. Fix: refuse a push from a non-default ref for proposals it didn't change against its merge-base, or refuse field regressions per record (title, tasksTotal and meta that differ from the stored values while the phase is behind). Add a test with a forked branch that has a newer commit time.
findings.scenario: At 10:00, main syncs FLT-101 with title 'Export v2'. Branch specclaw/102-x was cut at 09:00 and commits at 11:00 with FLT-101's title still 'Export'. Pushing it with --apply sets FLT-101's title back to 'Export'.

findings.message: The per-proposal stale mark (`meta.committedAt`) does not move forward reliably, so an older commit can still be applied. (a) When a newer push leaves a proposal unchanged, the row is skipped (`unchanged` → continue), so committedAt stays at the older time. (b) Every other writer replaces meta wholesale without committedAt: the self-sync (`syncSpecclaw` / bin.ts) and the `sync_proposal` tool. That removes the mark, and the next push from any older commit passes. Fix: keep the mark in its own column, or a per-project or per-proposal table, that every sync writes. Advance it even when the content is unchanged. Give the stale gate one source of truth.
findings.scenario: The stored FLT-101 title is 'A', last synced from a 10:00 commit. Branch X commits title 'B' at 11:00. Main's 12:00 push still says 'A', so it is unchanged and the mark stays at 10:00. Then X pushes at 11:00 and passes the stale check, and FLT-101 becomes 'B' even though a newer commit says 'A'.

findings.message: The project row lock protects the per-proposal checks but not the repo check. pushSpecclaw reads `repo_url` in its own transaction without a lock and compares it there. applyPush later takes `for update` on the project but never checks repo_url again. A relink that commits between the check and the apply lets a push from the repo that was just unlinked go through. Fix: compare repo_url inside applyPush, using the row it locks (`project.repo_url`), and refuse there.
findings.scenario: Push A from github.com/example/old passes the check. The PM then runs link_project_repo to set github.com/example/new, and that commits. Push A's apply still writes the old repo's specclaw state into the project.

findings.message: The concurrency test (`Promise.all([push(at(13)), push(at(14))])`) does not force the two pushes to overlap. If the 14:00 push finishes before the 13:00 push starts, the stale check refuses the 13:00 one and the test passes. If the 13:00 push runs first, the test also passes. Only a real overlap shows whether the lock in applyPush matters. Separately, upsertSpecProposal takes the same row lock on its first write, so deleting applyPush's early lock still leaves the test green most of the time. Fix: hold the first push's transaction open after it reads stored rows (a barrier, or a session holding the lock), start the second, and assert that it blocks. Then the test fails when the early `for update` is removed.
findings.scenario: With the `for update` at the top of applyPush deleted, the test still passes on most runs.

findings.message: `base.meta.pr ?? prior.pr` and `base.meta.verdict ?? prior.verdict` mean no push can ever clear a PR link or verdict. Main can't clear them either, because a missing value is treated the same as 'this branch doesn't know'. Fall back to the prior values only for non-default refs, or only when the record really omits the field.
findings.scenario: Main drops a superseded PR link from state.json and pushes. FLT-101 keeps showing the old PR.

findings.message: When dryRun is false and nothing is created or updated, the push returns `outcome: "applied"` and writes no sync_push row, even when every record was skipped as stale, as a step back, or as a held key. 'Nothing applied' and 'nothing new' now give the same answer. The README says 'Each applied or refused push is a delivery.sync_push row', yet a push refused record by record leaves no trace on the Repo sync card. Fix: return a distinct outcome (e.g. `skipped`/`nothing new`) and record a row when the skipped set contains anything other than the standing expected skips, or when it differs from the last recorded push.
findings.scenario: A lagging-branch push where every record comes back as `stale: last synced from a newer commit` returns {outcome:'applied', created:0, updated:0}. No row is written, and the PM's card shows no refused push.

findings.message: The test for the round-1 erasure blocker only checks `has_table_privilege` and runs an `update … where false`. It never drives the real erasure or purge path (core/privacy apply with the delivery.sync_push `anonymise` rule). It would stay green if the rule's fields, its subject columns or apply.ts's UPDATE didn't match the grant. Fix: open and complete an erasure for a person who pushed (or run purgeDue past P7Y), and assert that actor_id and for_user_id are nulled on their sync_push rows, for the actor-only, for_user-only and both-columns variants.
findings.scenario: Rename `for_user_id` in the retention entry's fields to a column apply.ts can't update. The test still passes, and erasure still fails at runtime.
